articles.title: $70 PS5 Game Now Available for $7
articles.summary: A PS5 game that normally costs $70 on the PlayStation Store is now available for $7 between now and December 1. This is the result of a gigantic 90% discount on the game. This is the biggest discount the game has ever received on the PS Store. Unfortunately, there is no PS4 version of the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A PS5 game that normally costs $70 on the PlayStation Store is now available for $7 between now and December 1. This is the result of a gigantic 90% discount on the game. This is the biggest discount the game has ever received on the PS Store. Unfortunately, there is no PS4 version of the game, so PS4 users will not be saving an easy $63 on one of 2023's best games and one of the best horror games of the PS5 generation.

Back in 2023, at the start of the year in January, developer Motive Studio and publisher EA released a remake of one of 2008's best games and the first release in a series that had been dormant since 2013. This game and series is Dead Space . The original game is often cited as one of the best horror games of all time, and one of the great games across all genres in its generation. To this end, the original earned an 89 on Metacritic back in the day, a very good score, especially for a horror game, as horror games tend to receive slightly lower reviews than many other genres. Fittingly, the remake earned the same score and cemented itself as one of the better remakes of this current generation . Not only is it a good remake, but the original experience simply still holds up with a graphical overhaul. And it's not just critics who think this, but PS5 users on the PlayStation Store as well, hence its 4.71 out of 5 stars after more than 46,000 user reviews.

EA doesn't discount most of its games beyond 90 percent. Some end up getting the 95% discount treatment, but it's typically in annualized or semi-annualized series. To this end, we do not expect Dead Space on PS5 to be cheaper than this until its base price gets a price drop.

A Sci-Fi Survival-Horror Classic For those entirely unfamiliar with the sci-fi survival-horror game, it puts you in control of Isaac Clarke, an everyman engineer sent to repair a colossal mining ship, the USG Ishimura. Upon arrival, though, it is clear something went terribly wrong. The ship's crew is dead, and Isaac's beloved partner, Nicole, is missing somewhere on the ship. Armed with just engineering tools, Isaac has to uncover what happened and find Nicole.

Those who end up checking out Dead Space on PS5 or PS5 Pro as a result of this PlayStation Store deal should expect a runtime of about 12 to 16 hours on average, and depending largely on playstyle. Completionists, though, will need closer to 60 hours with the game.

For those who don't have $7 to spare at the moment, there is a classic PS2 series now available on the PlayStation Store for $2.24 .

articles.title: J.A. Bayona, Guneet Monga Kapoor, Vikas Khanna Board Student Academy Award Winner 'The Dragon Letter' as Director Plans Feature Version (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Spanish director J.A. Bayona, Oscar-winning producer Guneet Monga Kapoor and Michelin-starred chef and filmmaker Vikas Khanna have come aboard short "The Dragon Letter" as executive producers, and Ladakhi director Stanzin Jigmet tells Variety he is developing a feature version of the Student Academy Award-winning short. articles.content:
Spanish director J.A. Bayona , Oscar-winning producer Guneet Monga Kapoor and Michelin-starred chef and filmmaker Vikas Khanna have come aboard short "The Dragon Letter" as executive producers, and Ladakhi director Stanzin Jigmet tells Variety he is developing a feature version of the Student Academy Award-winning short.

The film was named the narrative Gold winner at the 53rd Student Academy Awards, and has been entered in the live action short race for the 99th Academy Awards. Spain's ESCAC Films produced it in association with India Sikhya Entertainment, with shooting split between Ladakh and Barcelona. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Qatar’s Film Committee and Watermelon Pictures Forge Partnership to Co-Produce a Slate of Films From the 'Global South' ‘He Walked So I Could Run’: ‘Project Hail Mary’ Breakout James Ortiz on Andy Serkis, Becoming Rocky and the Art of Puppetry

Bayona was born in Barcelona, the city where Jigmet trained, and made his first feature with "The Orphanage." He went on to direct "The Impossible," "A Monster Calls," "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom" and "Society of the Snow."

"What I find so beautiful about 'The Dragon Letter' is how a deeply personal story, rooted in a remote corner of the Himalayas, can speak to something universal: friendship, kindness, and the courage to find your own voice," Bayona said.

"That, to me, is the magic of cinema. It brings us together, helps us make sense of our own little worlds, and gives us a language through which we can understand one another. The more deeply we explore what makes us unique, the more we discover what connects us to the rest of the world. Sometimes, the most universal stories are born in the most unexpected places."

A BAFTA nominee who co-founded Sikhya Entertainment, the Mumbai banner, Monga Kapoor won the documentary short Oscar in 2023 alongside director Kartiki Gonsalves for "The Elephant Whisperers," the first Indian production to take that award. She was also an executive producer on "Period. End of Sentence.," which won in the same category in 2019. France has made her a Chevalier de l'Ordre des Arts et des Lettres, and she set up Women in Film India to support women and gender-diverse professionals in the country's screen sector. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"What moved me most about 'The Dragon Letter' is its beautiful message about childhood friendship. When you're young, a friend who helps you with your homework or draws a dragon for you can make you feel understood in a way that stays with you for life. Stanzin captures that tenderness so honestly and reminds us how those small acts of kindness can give children the confidence to find their own voice. I'm delighted to come on board as executive producer and help share his film with audiences around the world," Monga Kapoor said.

For an independent filmmaker, Jigmet tells Variety , Monga Kapoor brings ties to publicists and a working knowledge of awards campaigns. "She has lots of experience and such a personality in championing this independent cinema and taking it to international stages. I'm really grateful that Guneet joined my project as an executive producer and helping us a lot," he says.

Khanna, who was raised in Amritsar, runs the kitchen at Bungalow in New York and is a judge on "MasterChef India." He has published 36 books and made several documentaries, and his Feed India initiative has helped provide millions of meals. His first feature as director, "The Last Color," starred Neena Gupta and centered on a friendship that grows between an older widow and a young tightrope walker in Varanasi.

"I love the way he shows how children look after one another in ways adults might barely notice," Khanna said.

The story centers on Skarma (Jigmet Spalchen), a 10-year-old who is asked to pen a note to his Barcelona sponsor. Every child in the class is supposed to copy out the same text and sketch the same dragon. Skarma has other ideas about what to say. The question is whether he can summon the nerve to write them down.

The film draws on Jigmet's own years at a Himalayan boarding school. Many of his friends there had sponsors in Europe and had to send them a thank-you letter every year. Jigmet would decorate those letters with a dragon, including for classmates who helped with his schoolwork.

He wrote the script at ESCAC in Barcelona, where every student on his master's program had to pitch a story to the school. Being in Spain already suited the project, since its final section had to be filmed in Europe.

Jigmet comes from Mulbekh, a Himalayan village without a cinema. "I grew up very far from the industry, so in Ladakh I learned filmmaking from YouTube only," he says. In 2021 he launched Ladakh-based Pixel Challenger Films, making ads and public awareness films, and he also worked on Vidhu Vinod Chopra's "12th Fail." A few of his narrative commercials went viral, and ESCAC got in touch offering him a scholarship for a master's in film directing. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

One of his professors there told the class: "Never do films with kids and dogs. You are going to struggle a lot." Jigmet went on to write a film with 75 children in it.

The Barcelona shoot, with a professional crew and professional actors, was "like a luxury for me," he says. Ladakh was another matter. There he worked with non-actors, an entire school of children and a very small team. Equipment was scarce, and local kids pitched in by holding the lights. Having grown up in the Himalayas within that culture, Jigmet says, he was able to draw natural performances from his young cast.

Jigmet lensed the Ladakh scenes himself and also edited the film. Miguel Esteban Alonso handled cinematography for the Barcelona unit. Sergi Casamitjana and Aintza Serra produced for ESCAC Films, with Pixel Challenger Films participating. Jigmet Wangial, Rosa Nicolás, Ferran Devick and Urgain Phuntsog round out the cast. Victor H. L. Bruneau was line producer, Natali Gutierrez production designer and Sebastián Orueta Murillo sound designer.

Sikhya, a Jio Studios company, has backed titles including "The Lunchbox," "Masaan," "Pagglait" and "Kill," along with Indian National Film Award winners "Kathal – A Jackfruit Mystery" and "Soorarai Pottru." Its latest theatrical releases are Karthik Subbaraj's "Dorothy" and "Udta Teer," the first feature from writer-director Akash Kaushik.

For now, Jigmet is busy with the short's Oscar campaign. "But I'm also developing a feature version of 'The Dragon Letter.' That's the plan," he says.

Jigmet is currently attending the WAVES Film Bazaar , the market component of the International Film Festival of India in Goa.

articles.title: Crunchyroll's Darkest Fall 2026 Anime Has Become the Perfect Zombie Anime
articles.summary: Image courtesy of 100studio Crunchyroll's darkest anime of Fall 2026 has become a zombie anime with the ideal setup, complementing the series' premise and making it even spookier and scarier. The zombie genre is famous across all forms of media, regardless of how it is presented. Many popular zombie anime have incorporated the genre as a comedic element. While […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Crunchyroll 's darkest anime of Fall 2026 has become a zombie anime with the ideal setup, complementing the series' premise and making it even spookier and scarier. The zombie genre is famous across all forms of media, regardless of how it is presented. Many popular zombie anime have incorporated the genre as a comedic element. While they still feature spooky and scary elements, what the darkest anime of Fall 2026 is doing is arguably among the scariest portrayals yet. The Vermilion Mask emerged as a spooky anime thanks to its intriguing premise, in which a mask's type determines the powers of its wearer.

The series has deliberately portrayed the masks' powers as dark and unsettling, establishing the anime's overall tone. Now, in the latest episode, The Vermilion Mask Episode 7, the series has introduced a mask user with arguably one of the most terrifying powers, elevating its horror elements even further. It introduces the Mask of Necromancy, which allows its user to control the dead, as its name suggests. However, the new villain is not simply another mask user but also has a devastating plan, unleashing an apocalyptic zombie outbreak that transforms The Vermilion Mask into a zombie survival action thriller with horror elements .

The Vermilion Mask Episode 7, titled "The Mask of Necromancy," introduces a new character named Rinne, who strangely first appears in Peru's dream before being revealed as the leader of the cult that worships the legendary mask maker Gaston. However, the episode later delivers a surprising revelation: Rinne is the user of the Mask of Necromancy, which is unveiled alongside two more striking details. The first is that this mask has a threat level of four, the same as the Mask of the Warrior God. While this alone is enough to shake Peru and his allies' confidence in how they would deal with it, the second detail reveals that Rinne is the master of this mask.

This means that Rinne and the mask share the same thoughts and desires, with both seeking the same goal: the destruction of humanity. It is now evident that, through the Mask of Necromancy, Rinne plans to gain control over the dead, with the mask also possessing the strange ability to manipulate living humans, as seen with Akane, a woman somehow connected to Peru's childhood. The setup for a horror scenario goes beyond what the series' previous arcs have presented, and with several other elements in play, this new arc has the potential to become the perfect zombie anime .

While the dead coming back to life and attempting to recruit others into their cult is one of the fun elements that gives the series a zombie-like presence, the introduction of Mok Sharib adds another layer. Despite possessing a spooky mask ability that makes him seem like a ghost, he is comically afraid of zombies and ghosts, adding a much-needed element of humor to the series. All in all, The Vermilion Mask has been doing exceptionally well with each arc, and the newest one introduces a zombie premise that perfectly complements the series' overall vibe. Crunchyroll's darkest anime of Fall 2026 has transformed into something incredibly versatile , making it a series that everyone should definitely be watching.

articles.title: Before Doomsday, I Haven't Forgotten Marvel's Dirtiest Trick With Avengers: Infinity War
articles.summary: Avengers: Doomsday is just around the corner, and I can't wait for the first half of the Multiverse Saga's epic two-part conclusion. Doomsday and Secret Wars will wrap up the last few years of the MCU, and if Doomsday is anything like its Infinity Saga equivalent, Avengers: Infinity War, I'm prepared for the film to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday is just around the corner, and I can't wait for the first half of the Multiverse Saga's epic two-part conclusion. Doomsday and Secret Wars will wrap up the last few years of the MCU, and if Doomsday is anything like its Infinity Saga equivalent, Avengers: Infinity War , I'm prepared for the film to be a tragedy .

However, this may not be the only parallel that Doomsday has with Infinity War . After all, I still remember the MCU's dirtiest Infinity War trick, and if Marvel Studios does the same thing this time around, I'll know that I can't trust them ever again.

Avengers: Infinity War was one of the most exciting movies ever made, and there was no stopping the hype train during the lead-up to its release. Thanos had been built up as the MCU's big bad since 2012's The Avengers , and the 2018 crossover film was finally set to properly show off the villain for the first time. The film was sure to be full of major firsts for the franchise, such as the Guardians of the Galaxy finally meeting the Avengers. The marketing for the film knew how to get fans excited, highlighting how everything had been building up to this.

However, when Infinity War finally hit theaters, I and many other fans realized that the marketing for the film was a bit deceptive. Multiple elements from the trailers were not included in the final film, something that isn't uncommon. For example, the Thanos line “Fun isn’t something one considers when balancing the universe, but this does put a smile on my face,” doesn't appear in the movie, as it was replaced by another line during post-production.

As it turns out, though, one shot was entirely invented for the trailer. A hero shot shows Captain America, Hulk, Black Panther , and several other characters running directly at the camera, presumably during the Battle of Wakanda. However, Hulk had already stopped coming out at this point. The Russos have since confirmed that the hero shot was created solely for marketing purposes and was presumably designed to mislead fans (via Collider ). Considering that this was one of the most epic shots from the trailer, its exclusion from the final film was a bit disappointing for fans. After all, we didn't know that it was a fake shot at the time.

Marvel Studios has tampered with trailer footage multiple times since Infinity War , hiding characters and other elements in order to keep surprises safe for the final film. This is a good thing, as the amount of marketing materials that blockbusters of this scale require means that a good chunk of each movie's footage would have to be released ahead of time. So, in order to keep surprise heroes and story beats secret, Marvel needs to trick fans occasionally.

However, this does mean that we need to remember that MCU trailer footage can't be trusted. Avengers: Doomsday 's trailers have shown a surprising amount of footage in the lead-up to the film. While we don't know much about the story, we have seen an Avengers vs. X-Men fight, Thor fighting Doom, the return of Sentinels, the confirmation of multiple incursions, and so much more. These elements seem like way too much to reveal ahead of time, even if Doomsday has other secrets in store.

It is entirely possible that any of these moments are fake, whether they be shots entirely created for the trailer or shots that have been altered for marketing purposes. Characters could be hidden, settings could be changed, and shots could be invented. While it is likely that some of Doomsday 's trailer footage is real, it is also likely that all of it isn't.

We won't know what's real and what's fake in Doomsday 's trailers until the film hits theaters, and it'll be interesting to analyze the film's marketing in retrospect. Marvel Studios has had years to perfect the art of hooking audience members without giving too much away, and hopefully they have found the perfect balance here. After all, Doomsday has received less narrative buildup than the conclusion of the Infinity Saga did. Thus, Marvel has to convince old viewers to come back while still keeping enough surprises to make the viewing experience worth it.

What Avengers: Doomsday trailer shots do you think are fake? Let us know on the ComicBook Forum !

articles.title: New Free Nintendo Switch Game Now Available on the eShop
articles.summary: A new, free Nintendo Switch game has been released on the Nintendo eShop. It's not common for free games to be released on the eShop, and when it does happen, it's usually a free-to-play game stuffed with microtransactions or the biggest shovelware game in the history of shovelware. This new free Nintendo Switch game is […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new, free Nintendo Switch game has been released on the Nintendo eShop. It's not common for free games to be released on the eShop, and when it does happen, it's usually a free-to-play game stuffed with microtransactions or the biggest shovelware game in the history of shovelware. This new free Nintendo Switch game is nothing special, but it doesn't fall into these two categories. That said, it is worth noting that there is no Nintendo Switch 2 version of the game, so those on the newer Nintendo console will have to settle for playing the Switch version via backward compatibility.

The new free Nintendo Switch game just released on the Nintendo eShop is a new geography game from developer QubicGames called Geo Book . It's unclear what Nintendo users think of it so far because the Nintendo eShop does not have user reviews. The game is also on PS5, though, and the PlayStation Store does have user reviews. And its user reviews on the PlayStation Store aren't amazing, but they aren't bad either. To this end, it has 151 user reviews so far from PS5 users, with a score of 3.58 out of 5 stars. On a 100-point scale, this is a semi-decent score of 72. Across these 151 user reviews, the most common review is a 5/5, with 55% of the share. The second most common is 1/5, though, with 26% of the share.

It is worth noting that while the new Nintendo Switch game is available for free, there is a premium version that expands upon the game.

For those interested in the free Nintendo Switch game, it is pitched as a geography game that turns exploring the world into a fun adventure. In it, you will explore across the world's continents, discover fascinating locations, and challenge your memory. Obviously, a knowledge of geography will also be put to the test across various mini-games.

It's a free game, so obviously it's not incredible, but for those on a budget who also enjoy geography, it's worth looking into. Those with a little bit of change to spare, meanwhile, will find an $80 Nintendo Switch game discounted on the Nintendo eShop to just $8 , thanks to a massive 90% discount that is live until next month. Meanwhile, to go with this free game is a new promotion directly from Nintendo for some free Nintendo Switch Online .

articles.title: SNL Fans Thought The Show Was Building Around Ashley Padilla, But Not So Fast
articles.summary: She's getting her time to shine, but it's not turning into the Ashley Padilla show.
articles.content:
Much of the conversation around Saturday Night Live last season was about Ashley Padilla. In just her sophomore turn, the comedian emerged as a clear breakout star and was the subject of numerous positive articles and think pieces about how she was becoming the face of the show. There was even a fair bit of outrage about the fact that she wasn’t promoted from featured player to full cast member mid-season. Most SNL fans, myself included, assumed Lorne Michaels and the writers would double down and fully build around her this season, potentially at the expense of other cast members, but six episodes in, the numbers are telling a different story.

That’s not just the eyetest either. The Saturday Night Network released its tally of sketch appearances over the course of the first six episodes, and Padilla is one of six cast members that is sitting between 23 and 25. Here’s the list…

Now, to be clear, this is in no way an indictment of Padilla or an accusation that she’s anything less than brilliant. I think this season has been another step forward for her. Despite trailing in total sketches, she’s actually first in total screentime and has had quite a few buzzy moments already. She’s just as terrific as ever and will almost certainly continue to be one of the main characters, but it’s worth acknowledging that everyone else is getting a chance to eat too .

articles.title: 5 Of The Best Sci-Fi Movies From This Century Are All Streaming In The Same Place
articles.summary: Get the popcorn ready and strap in!
articles.content:
We've gotten some truly great sci-fi movies in the first quarter of this century, and I realized recently that five of the absolute best ones are all streaming in the same place. Whether its characters are traveling through space, trying to solve mysteries or trapped in a time look, each of the movies I'm about to talk about are must-sees, and more importantly, must-see again and again.

And with that, let's get on to the list of five of the best sci-fi movies from this century, all of which are streaming on Paramount+.

Christopher Nolan 's epic movie sees Matthew McConaughey leaving his family behind to help an astronaut crew search for a new planet for mankind when Earth becomes uninhabitable. For a movie that's nearly three hours, Interstellar still manages to pace itself perfectly, while also balancing great character arcs, spectacular sci-fi visuals, a complex plot and a suspenseful build-up right to the end. Also, with actors like McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Michael Caine, Jessica Chastain and John Lithgow, the cast is sensational.

Amy Adams and Jeremy Renner star as two people brought in to try to translate the language of aliens who've recently invaded the planet. The words "intense," "emotional," "dramatic," and "spectacular" don't feel big enough to describe Denis Villeneuve 's movie. Not only is Arrival one of the best sci-fi movies of all time , but it's one of my all-time favorite films, period. Years later, I still think about the ending of this movie .

Not to state the obvious, but sci-fi movies don't get nearly enough Academy Awards recognition. Gravity , fortunately, is a bit of an exception. Alfonso Cuarón 's outstanding sci-fi thriller starring Sandra Bullock and George Clooney had us all on the edge of our seats in theaters, and then again on Oscar night after it received 10 nominations (it missed Best Picture, but did win several other categories, including Director). This story of survival follows two astronauts trying to get back to Earth after a disaster strikes their shuttle. In addition to its great performances, Gravity also has some truly astounding special effects .

One of two Tom Cruise sci-fi movies on this list (and one of three mentioned), Steven Spielberg 's Minority Report is set in a future where a metropolitan police department uses a predictive system involving psychics and technology to anticipate and prevent crime before it happens, detaining the murderers before they actually commit their crime. Cruise's character is a detective who pursues the would-be criminals, but ends up being pursued himself when the precogs predict he's about to commit a murder. There's action, mystery, and a lot of cool, futuristic technology in this one.

While most of the movies on this list come with a rather serious tone, I'd be remiss if I excluded Edge of Tomorrow just because it's full of alien battle chaos. Doug Liman's action-sci-fi movie is very much a popcorn flick, but in the best possible way. Tom Cruise plays a military officer who's forced into combat during a war waged on an invading species. When he finds himself stuck in a time loop, which resets the day every time he dies (and that happens a lot), he partners with Emily Blunt's character to try to find a way through it. It's exciting, full of action and big alien war scenes. It's even a bit funny at times.

Of course, if you want to make a Tom Cruise sci-fi trilogy out of your day, you can do just that, as Paramount+ also has Spielberg's War of the Worlds available streaming . While many would agree that Amazon's recent book-to-screen adaptation of H.G. Wells' sci-fi classic is not good, the 2005 movie starring Cruise and Dakota Fanning holds up rather nicely.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Has a Chance to Finally Rectify GTA 5’s Greatest Failure
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has taken the gaming industry by storm and is proving to be one of Rockstar Games' greatest accomplishments. With a 99 aggregate score on Metacritic, it is hard not to praise the game even with its decade of expectations. While the technical achievements and incredible attention to detail throughout Vice City […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Grand Theft Auto 6 has taken the gaming industry by storm and is proving to be one of Rockstar Games' greatest accomplishments. With a 99 aggregate score on Metacritic , it is hard not to praise the game even with its decade of expectations. While the technical achievements and incredible attention to detail throughout Vice City and Leonida deserve recognition, Rockstar has also delivered an engaging story with characters that draw you in. Jason and Lucia have the potential to be the best protagonists in the series, and they should show that Rockstar should invest in them, something it failed to do for Grand Theft Auto 5's protagonists.

As much as I enjoyed Grand Theft Auto 5 , I've always been disappointed that Rockstar never expanded on Michael, Franklin, and Trevor's stories. GTA Online's success changed the game's trajectory and led Rockstar to abandon the promised single-player DLC. With how successful GTA Online , it isn't a surprise, but it still remains a disappointment. The same cycle happened with Red Dead Redemption 2 , and it cannot happen with GTA 6 . With Grand Theft Auto 6 placing so much emphasis on the relationship between Jason and Lucia, Rockstar cannot afford to make the same mistake again. Single-player DLC needs to be part of its future.

Over a decade ago, after completing GTA 5's story, I was beyond excited to continue the single-player through DLC. In December 2013, Rockstar announced plans for substantial story additions in 2014 that would continue the adventures of Michael, Franklin, and Trevor. Yet, those additions never came to be, largely in part because of GTA Online . Los Santos' future took a direction where multiplayer, shark cards, and the series embraced a live-service model.

In 2017, Rockstar design director Imran Sarwar explained why single-player expansions never happened. The resources required to bring GTA 5 to newer consoles, support GTA Online , and develop Red Dead Redemption 2 made producing additional story content difficult. Rockstar also considered the original campaign sufficiently complete. While these were understandable reasons, they honestly felt like an excuse to support GTA Online because it was a constant source of revenue.

Watching Los Santos evolve through multiplayer updates made the absence of single-player DLC increasingly frustrating. New vehicles, locations, characters, and criminal enterprises gave players countless reasons to return, provided they were interested in multiplayer. I wanted to experience that evolving world through the characters I had already grown attached to. Complete or not, Rockstar Games could easily have expanded Los Santos and the narrative it constructed with single-player DLC.

What makes Grand Theft Auto 6 work so well is its emphasis on the relationship between Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Their reliance on one another gives the story its heart and has drawn players in. Both have interesting backgrounds that help drive the narrative, and Rockstar Games has taken its time to explore these fully. From the opening moments, I was invested in the game, and though I have not finished the story yet, I absolutely want to see more. An expansion wouldn't necessarily need to continue the main campaign, as it could be set in previous times in the characters' lives as well.

I'd love to experience an expansion exploring Lucia's life before prison or Jason's early involvement with drug runners in the Leonida Keys. Either could offer a different perspective on the characters while developing relationships that shaped their lives before the events of GTA 6 . Rockstar could also introduce entirely new protagonists, allowing players to experience familiar locations and encounters through the eyes of someone operating outside the central narrative.

Rockstar already demonstrated how effective this approach could be with Grand Theft Auto 4 . Its two expansions, The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony , explored different sides of Liberty City's criminal underworld through Johnny Klebitz and Luis Lopez. Both stories intersected with Niko Bellic's adventure while maintaining distinct identities. This is an easy route the studio can take with GTA 6, and it wouldn't detract from the main narrative. The original story is already full of interesting characters and moments, and I know players would love to see more.

There's little reason to expect Rockstar Games to abandon the multiplayer model that proved so successful with its previous release. GTA 6 Online could become another enormously popular multiplayer experience, potentially entertaining players for years. But this doesn't mean the studio should abandon the single-player experience. There is a timeline in which both can get the support they need to satisfy all GTA fans, even if it is just a one-time DLC release, though multiple would be preferred.

Not every story expansion needs to rival the size of a standalone Rockstar game, either. A smaller, focused campaign utilizing Leonida's existing environments could deliver a compelling reason to return to the game without requiring an entirely new map. I'd love to see an expansion that adds new detailed missions, memorable characters, and new criminal activities. Quality storytelling matters considerably more to me than another hundred hours of activities scattered across an already enormous open world.

Ultimately, Grand Theft Auto 6 's extraordinary reception shows that single-player works really should compel Rockstar to support it. Players shouldn't have to wait another decade or longer to experience more GTA in GTA 7 . Multiplayer certainly provides longevity, but it is not for everyone, and the studio's handcrafted narratives offer something fundamentally different. Rockstar has invested years into creating Leonida and developing Jason and Lucia, and it would be a shame not to continue that through DLC.

articles.title: I Just Found Out The Real Reason Young Sheldon Wasn’t Filmed Before A Live Audience Like The Big Bang Theory
articles.summary: It's a shrewd choice, but I get it.
articles.content:
The Big Bang Theory may be a popular and highly regarded sitcom on its own but, at this point, it’s also spawned multiple spinoffs that have cumulatively led to the formation of a franchise. Of course, the first offshoot from the Chuck Lorre and Bill Prady-created sitcom was Young Sheldon , which debuted in 2017. Aside from having tonal differences from Big Bang , the series also had a single-camera set-up as opposed to a multi-cam one with a live audience. I always wondered why that was the case and, now, I finally have my answer.

So, apparently, Lorre, along with co-showrunners Steven Molaro and Steve Holland, sought a somewhat more personal vibe for this show that didn’t quite mesh with the breakneck pace of a multi-camera comedy. While I’m someone who has long enjoyed situation comedies that have live audiences, even I can understand the rationale here. There are just some stories that lend themselves better to the single camera format. And that’s not the only reason for Young Sheldon ’s changing things up from its famous predecessor:

I’d imagine that for an actor of any age it can be a little daunting to act in front of a live audience, and doing so is also tedious. Based on Lorre’s sentiments, I imagine that was his thinking in regard to choosing the format for YS. Plenty of current and former child actors (including many still working today) have, of course, given excellent performances on multi-camera sitcoms. Still, I can definitely understand how working with young performers in a more controlled environment would be easier for them and the crew.

articles.title: 3 X-Men Villains That Actually Need Their Own Movies in the MCU, Because Fox Wasted Them

While Marvel Studios' track record isn't as good as its diehard fans like to claim, it's better than 20th Century […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The X-Men are coming to the Marvel Cinematic Universe and even the most curmudgeonly X-fans who aren't super into the MCU anymore are pretty excited (I have no idea who that could be referring to). While Marvel Studios' track record isn't as good as its diehard fans like to claim, it's better than 20th Century Fox's, the former home of the X-Men's film rights. While there are some excellent FoX-Men movies, there are also a lot of missteps from the 19 years of Fox movies we got. Some of the most disappointing parts of the films are the villains that the studio wasted. This is especially egregious because the X-Men have some of the greatest villains ever .

While the MCU isn't exactly the best at villains either, it can't be worse than Fox. However, some X-villains need more than just to make appearances to make up for what Fox did to them. They need their own movies to make up for it, with these three X-Men villains especially needing a solo MCU movie.

Emma Frost has become integral to the X-Men , but if the MCU is going to use the White Queen, they should follow the comics and introduce her as a villain first. Well, and give her a movie. Fox introduced Emma Frost in X-Men: First Class and cast Mad Men 's January Jones to play her. Fans were excited to see her play the blond telepath, but they honestly shouldn't have been. Jones isn't a bad actress by any stretch of the imagination, but her role in the movie was almost non-existent. I don't know if director Matthew Vaughan just didn't give her good direction or if the script had her a one-note character who never even changed her facial expression, but the performance we got was the opposite of good.

Emma Frost is a legendary character and Fox made her boring. Every fan of Emma knows that if there's one thing that she can't tolerate, it's boredom. Emma's back story is super interesting – she was born to a family of backstabbing rich people with mental problems and mutant powers, she ran away from home to the Hellfire Club, and worked her way up to the White Queen. That's a movie that any fans would want to see and it would set her up for her eventual battles against the X-Men – and her later tenure with the group – perfectly.

Juggernaut is one of the X-Men's oldest villains and currently a member of the team. Cain Marko was the stepbrother of Charles Xavier and he hated the wealthy son of privilege, constantly bullying him. Eventually, he'd find the Crimson Gem of Cyttorak and become the unstoppable Juggernaut. In the movies, he showed up out of nowhere in X3: The Last Stand , said one of the most memed lines ever (you know what it is), and did nothing else. There was no mention of his relationship with Xavier and they didn't even try to explain his powers, instead depending on the fact that viewers probably knew enough about the group to know who he was and what his deal was.

Juggernaut was completely wasted by Fox and the MCU needs to make that right. In the comics, Cain was a soldier when he found the Crimson Gem, so maybe we could get that – Cain in army, possibly in the Middle East, finding the Gem and becoming Juggernaut. Maybe he has to kill his fellow soldiers to get it or something. Or maybe the movie is about him learning to deal with his new powers and their dark master. Or they can just make a movie where he fights the Hulk, because that would be cool. Juggernaut deserves something to make up for what Fox did to him.

Wolverine and Sabretooth have the X-Men's most brutal rivalry , so fans were excited when it was announced he was going to be a part of 2000's X-Men . Played by wrestler Tyler Mane, the villain was… certainly a villain in a superhero movie. He looked the part, but it was the most nothingburger performance (well, until Jones' Emma Frost). Sabretooth is a beloved villain, an entertaining monster who was as skilled with his tongue as he was with his claws. He would tear you apart verbally while tearing you apart with his bare hands. However, the movie version was the most lackluster ever.

The villain appeared again in X-Men Origins: Wolverine , a movie which is the worst Wolverine movie but somehow has the best Sabretooth. Liev Schreiber was perfect in the role, nailing the monstrous glee of Victor Creed. Fox was 1 for 2 with Sabretooth and although they found the perfect actor for the villain, they never brought him back. Honestly, the fact that we never got more Schreiber Sabretooth is worse than the Mane Sabretooth and for that, we deserve a Sabretooth movie to make up for it, starring Schreiber, who would still make an amazing Victor Creed (that a lot of Sabreteeth in one sentence). Make it happen, Marvel.

What Fox X-Men villains do you think deserve their own movie? Do you think Fox did a good job with any of the villains? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Home Alone Director Says a Legacy Sequel Is Impossible Now But Macaulay Culkin Is Making One Anyway
articles.summary: 20th Century Studios 36 years after the original movie was released, a new entry in the Home Alone franchise is officially on the way with Macaulay Culkin reprising the character of Kevin McCallister. The news broke yesterday with Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg reportedly attached to the feature film as both writers and producers, along with the shocking […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google 36 years after the original movie was released, a new entry in the Home Alone franchise is officially on the way with Macaulay Culkin reprising the character of Kevin McCallister. The news broke yesterday with Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg reportedly attached to the feature film as both writers and producers, along with the shocking news that Culkin would return to the breakout role that changed the trajectory of his life and career in many ways — good and bad. All of this happened in the blink of an eye, but as this hot story was developing, a different one had just occurred that told a different side of the story.

Shifting this momentous surprise into something a little more unexpected, the first director for the franchise had just done an interview minutes before the news broke explaining why a legacy sequel could never happen for a very valid reason. Unbeknownst to him, the cogs had been turning in the Disney machine for some time and a new movie had been development with this director left completely in the dark. It's the ultimate example of bad timing, but if his comments hold any weight to them — and they do — this new Home Alone could have an uphill battle in grabbing eyes on it, as well as a tougher struggle in being as successful as the original.

Chris Columbus is the prototype for the type of director who can take a children's film and instill heart and sentimentality into its story while also making something mature yet accessible. If anyone understands the art of moviemaking for this broad but niche audience, it's Columbus. That may be the reason he spoke with his chest during a recent interview with a media outlet while discussing the topic of Home Alone , a series that has been making the rounds lately as Culkin reprised the character for a McDonald's collaboration , fueling rumors that the actor might be looking to restart the franchise. His primary reason for nixing any rumors of a sequel? The loss of one of its other stars, Catherine O'Hara.

“Catherine, as I’ve always said, is 50% of Home Alone ,” Columbus told Variety . “There’s the yin and yang of Home Alone : Catherine O’Hara and Macaulay Culkin. Without those two in the film, there is no film, because they create the emotional epicenter of that film.” O'Hara sadly passed away earlier this year i n January, leaving behind a prolific legacy of work as well as being a genuinely great human being. “It was really about Catherine and Macaulay, if anyone ever wanted to do a sequel,” Columbus continued, “and unfortunately that can’t happen now.”

“I think you potentially could still entertain the idea of doing another Home Alone with the cast,” Columbus added in regards to ways another Home Alone without O'Hara could work, but wasn't optimistic. “Not any of these ridiculous follow-ups to the first. And I only say ridiculous because it’s weird with filmmakers. They don’t understand why that cast works so well. It’s always about the cast. It’s like The Goonies . It’s about the cast.”

His take on a new movie makes perfect sense, but the cherry on top of this story is what happened next. A few moments prior to doing the interview with Variety, the news broke that Culkin was indeed returning to the franchise with the announcement of Rogen and Goldberg behind it. According to the report from his interviewer, "Columbus had no knowledge that the project was in development or about to be announced." His dance card has filled up already as he prepares to direct Gremlins 3 over 30 years since the first was released, which begins shooting early in 2027. When pressed after the announcement for a follow-up, Columbus declined to comment further.

Culkin has been on the record several times regarding the Home Alone series in recent years, even laying out the foundation for a script that he felt was the best way to bring back his nostalgic character while opening the door for the next generation of young audience members. Its this pitch that seems to be what the upcoming movie will be about, or at least use as part of its core. In that version, O'Hara's performance is not a mandatory part of the story and may even add more gravity to the drama of it all, but her presence would be sorely missed. We will see how they honor the memory of O'Hara when this movie is released, although a date and additional information has yet to be revealed.

Is Chris Columbus right about how a new Home Alone wouldn't work as well without O'Hara, or does Culkin's idea for a new film make sense without her? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: James McAvoy's Forgotten Comic Book Movie Is Secretly One of His Best, And the Cast Is Stacked With Legends
articles.summary: When people think of James McAvoy and comic book movies, their minds rightfully go right to his role as Professor Charles Xavier. McAvoy played the iconic leader of the X-Men in several prequel films, starting with X-Men: First Class. His portrayal of the character lived up to what the legendary Patrick Stewart first did and […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When people think of James McAvoy and comic book movies, their minds rightfully go right to his role as Professor Charles Xavier. McAvoy played the iconic leader of the X-Men in several prequel films, starting with X-Men: First Class . His portrayal of the character lived up to what the legendary Patrick Stewart first did and helped establish him as a major player in Hollywood. That said, before truly breaking out as Professor X, James McAvoy can trace his comic book film roots back a few years prior to one of the most underrated action flicks of the 2000s, Wanted .

Loosely based on a comic book miniseries of the same name, Wanted was the kind of thing that grabbed audiences even if they didn't know it was based on a comic book series. Wanted played a key part in the growing and impressive career of James McAvoy, yet it is so much more than that. The film is also an easily rewatchable blast of a project that happens to feature one of the best casts of its time. McAvoy works alongside future breakout actors, Academy Award winners, and legitimate legends of the big screen. With so many notable stars, it's surprising that the film has been forgotten over the years.

When Wanted came out in 2008, it was one of those cases where a movie featured a lot of big names, yet the lead actor was something of an unknown. At that point in his career, McAvoy, who plays Wesley Allan Gibson, was best known for his short run on the original U.K. version of Shameless , as Mr. Tumnus in The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe , and in the critically acclaimed Atonement . However, those films were aimed at far different audiences than what Wanted was pulling in. This film allowed McAvoy the chance to showcase his skills in the action genre.

The one thing most people remember about Wanted is that it's the movie where people could curve bullets. The cool concept stuck with viewers, yet it's actually not even something pulled from the comics. In fact, the term "loosely based" is as clear as ever here because the comics are significantly different from the film. It's more vulgar and has more defined superheroes and villains, while the film introduces so many unique elements. Still, the movie adaptation was indeed action-packed and people rushed to see it to the tune of a box office intake of over $340 million.

Reviews for Wanted were also solid, and although a sequel was ultimately canceled, the film put a bunch of new eyes on James McAvoy. It also started a trend for him as some of his biggest roles are in the realm of superheroes. He may never have landed the part of Professor X without Wanted . McAvoy also famously played a man with 23 different identities in Split and Glass , which are unique takes on the superhero genre. There's also his part in Atomic Blonde , which is based on a graphic novel, and the underrated His Dark Materials , which is based on a novel series but has a lot of superhero elements in its story.

The fact that Wanted isn't a movie that's better remembered is a bit shocking given everything. Along with a lead who has since become a star, a great premise, and a strong box office, Wanted boasts a tremendous cast. The biggest name at the time was Angelina Jolie, who was in the midst of a great run. She plays Fox, a member of the Fraternity who mentors McAvoy's Wesley. Their scenes together are some of the film's best, yet Jolie is far from the only star to share the screen with McAvoy.

The iconic Morgan Freeman has a part as Mr. Sloan, the experienced leader and one of the founders of the Fraternity. Anytime you get Freeman in your film, you know it's going to be something special. Common, an underrated actor, appears as a weapons trainer known as the Gunsmith, while Terence Stamp plays Pekwarsky, a master at killing. Wanted even features an early appearance by Chris Pratt , who obviously went on to play Star-Lord in the MCU. He's just here for a small part as Wesley's friend, as this was even before he made a name for himself on Parks and Recreation .

There is simply so much to love about Wanted . The stellar cast is a blend of veteran performers and rising stars, the action is just fun to watch, and it helped set the tone for the rest of James McAvoy's career. It deserves to be better remembered than it is and any comic book action fan should check it out.

articles.title: James Bond 26: What Denis Villeneuve's Favorite Bond Movies Can Tell Us About His Plans for the Franchise
articles.summary: After watching every James Bond movie, it can start to feel like you’ve had one shaken martini too many. We’ve seen the world saved, women seduced by Bond’s accent, and some awful things happen to the MI6 agent. 007 has traversed the globe, from sinister island lairs to the underwater city of Atlantis. And every […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google After watching every James Bond movie, it can start to feel like you’ve had one shaken martini too many. We’ve seen the world saved, women seduced by Bond’s accent, and some awful things happen to the MI6 agent. 007 has traversed the globe, from sinister island lairs to the underwater city of Atlantis. And every time a new actor plays Bond, he offers a fresh interpretation, while every new director must go through the same thought experiment: How do you make James Bond feel fresh without losing what made him the original 007?

Denis Villeneuve might just have the answer. As a kid, he watched Sean Connery’s Bond adventures with his father, and he’s held onto those memories for decades. He’s also named two Daniel Craig pictures among his favorites. That makes for a promising combination. Let’s dive into the films he enjoys most and see if we can get an idea of what Villeneuve has in store for the new 007 movie.

The director has shared that Casino Royale is one of his favorite Bond adventures. Craig's first Bond film ditched the sci-fi tech and off-the-rack villainy of previous entries in favor of something grittier and more realistic. Director Martin Campbell turned Craig loose to bleed, make mistakes, and occasionally be miserable on the job. Years later, Villeneuve named it as one of his favorite movies of all time. He's also said that he revisited the Bond franchise during difficult periods in his life. That's a pretty high recommendation for any cinematic franchise, let alone one centered on international intrigue and really expensive car insurance.

Daniel Craig isn't my favorite Bond, but his era definitely changed the way we see James Bond. I'm more partial to the classics like Connery and Moore, and especially my personal favorite, Pierce Brosnan. And here's the trailer for Casino Royale to serve as a quick reminder—and preview—of what the James Bond 26 movie might be like in tone and style.

As for Skyfall , Villeneuve appreciates that director Sam Mendes took Craig's performance somewhere even darker. It explored the bond between 007 and his boss and pondered whether spies still had a place in the modern world. The action was loud, but it was also tonally significant. Together, the two films give us an idea of where his interest might lie. Villeneuve seems to be drawn toward Bond stories that delve into the man behind the tuxedo. That's not to say every Daniel Craig Bond film followed the same approach, but his later adventures understood who Craig's 007 was underneath his bow tie. That's what makes those two films so interesting.

Sean Connery's Bond also factors into the director's vision since he grew up watching his childhood hero alongside his father. This iteration is known for the swaggering, sharp-suited 007 that Connery brought to the role. His Bond oozed charm and confidence, effortlessly putting people at ease—while being both humorous and dangerous. That take on James Bond is also distinctly consistent with what the filmmaker has said about the kind of 007 he believes in. That's a slightly dangerous man with an eye for trouble, a keen sense of humor, and the strength to get the job done. Think of it as all the qualities that define him wrapped up in one elegant package.

Villeneuve also remembers that James Bond is a spy with a license to kill. This means there could be doses of sensuality, intelligence, humor, and self-interest. Now there's a beautiful recipe when you consider his Blade Runner 2049 endeavor. Villeneuve knows how to take audiences on spectacular journeys while keeping the human experience at the center. He's also a filmmaker willing to take risks and shake up what we've come to expect from previous franchises. It sounds like there's a brew in the works with Connery's humor and Craig's intensity. Those elements could set the stage for whatever Villeneuve has in mind for the MI6 agent's next outing. After all, there's simply no need to make another Casino Royale , even if James Bond 26 goes back to the beginning.

Villeneuve has all the ingredients to make Bond 26 feel like a fresh adventure without forgetting the character's long history. Maybe he'll even introduce a new kind of martini. Not shaken or stirred, but pureed in a sandworm's digestive tract. What do you think the next James Bond should be like, and which elements of 007's past would you like Villeneuve to bring back? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: One of TV's Weirdest Unsolved Mysteries Happened 39 Years Ago, And Doctor Who Is a Forgotten Piece Of It
articles.summary: When people think of television mysteries in the 1980s, there are a few things that come to mind. We’re not talking mystery as a genre; we’re talking about actual questions that viewers were left pondering, things like who shot J.R. on Dallas, who survived the plane crash on Falcon Crest, who survived the massacre at […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When people think of television mysteries in the 1980s, there are a few things that come to mind. We’re not talking mystery as a genre; we’re talking about actual questions that viewers were left pondering, things like who shot J.R. on Dallas , who survived the plane crash on Falcon Crest , who survived the massacre at the royal wedding on Dynasty , and even will Sam Beckett ever make the leap home on Quantum Leap . But while those are big fictional mysteries, there’s a real-life mystery that happened 39 years ago today that remains unsolved — and Doctor Who played an unexpected part.

On the evening of November 22, 1987 — which, ironically, was also a Sunday — two Chicago television stations found their programming disrupted in one of the most bizarre moments ever. While one station, WGN-TV had settled in for the news and PBS affiliate WTTW settled in for Doctor Who, both broadcasts were briefly interrupted by a bootleg version of one of the most iconic pop culture figures of the day: Max Headroom. Here’s how it went down.

The bizarre Max Headroom incident was actually two hijackings in one night and it started on Chicago’s WGN-TV. At 9:14 p.m. during the sports segment of the station’s The Nine O’clock News, the regular broadcast went black for viewers at home for roughly 15 seconds before returning only it wasn’t the sports they got back. It was a weird broadcast of someone wearing a Max Headroom mask and sunglasses sitting in front of a metal panel. The set up was meant to look like the infamous real Max Headroom. This imposter, however, moved around erratically and the broadcast had no sound other than static and a weird, garbled buzzing. It lasted for just 30 seconds before station engineers were able to cut it off and restore the regular broadcast, which continued sports anchor Dan Roan quipping “Well, if you’re wondering what’s happened, so am I.”

So, you might be asking how Doctor Who is involved with this and that comes about two hours after the WGN-TV hijack. While viewers of local PBS station WTTW were settled in watching the Doctor Who serial “Horror of Fang Rock”, at around11:20 p.m. the faux Max Headroom appeared again but this time it got weird. The audio worked this time, with the figure making random comments, cultural references, strange noises and more. There was weird, random moaning, some rude gestures, feigned defecation, and it ended with his partial bare butt being struck with a flyswatter by a woman wearing a French maid costume. 90 seconds later, it was all over and Doctor Who returned .

As you can imagine, the two hijackings didn’t exactly amuse everyone. The government in particular wasn’t thrilled and the FCC went to work trying to track down the culprits. The FBI also got involved and the consequences for those responsible would have been serious — a $100,000 penalty (in 1980s money), a year in jail, or possibly both. The consequences were so steep because what the fake Max Headroom had done was a violation of federal law. This sort of thing also wasn’t the first time people had seen television broadcasts hijacked. In 1986 there was the so-called Captain Midnight incident in which satellite tech John MacDougall jammed HBO’s satellite signal during the broadcast of The Falcon and the Snowman to broadcast a message for four and a half minutes protesting HBO’s pricing. That act was considered “video terrorism,” prompting change in the law.

But while MacDougall was caught, whoever was behind Max Headroom never was. Despite a significant investigation, the identities of those involve has never been determined. There has been plenty of speculation, much of it centered around possible disgruntled employees or former employees of WGN or the Chicago underground hacker community or others, but nothing has ever panned out. Even with the statute of limitations for the crime running out in 1992 and therefore there being no consequences for owning up to it after that date, no one has come forward. The truth is we might never know who was behind this wild, weird moment in television history — but it is also something that can’t happen again. It was already hard enough to pull of the hijack in 1987 with experts suggesting that it would have required a lot of transmitting power and close proximity to the broadcast towers of both impacted stations in downtown Chicago, but in 2009 television stations in the U.S. changed over from analog signals to digital.

Do you think we’ll ever know who was behind the wild Max Headroom hijacking? Let us know your thoughts and your theories in the comments.

articles.title: Every Marvel Movie That Secretly Set Up Doctor Doom's MCU Arrival, Even If It Wasn’t Planned

After all, Thanos had cameos in multiple Avengers movies, while Doom seems like a last-minute substitute for Kang. However, this […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Doctor Doom is finally arriving in the MCU in Avengers: Doomsday , and one of the most common criticisms ahead of the film's release is that Doom hasn't been set up well enough by the franchise. After all, Thanos had cameos in multiple Avengers movies, while Doom seems like a last-minute substitute for Kang.

However, this isn't actually the case. According to Kevin Feige, the introduction of Doom was the plan all along . So, here is every MCU movie that set up Doom's arrival, not counting TV shows like VisionQuest .

One of the most shocking announcements regarding Doomsday was the inclusion of FOX's X-Men characters. While they have appeared in recent projects, like Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and Deadpool & Wolverine , their inclusion in Doom's debut film didn't seem obvious. However, for fans of the 2023 film The Marvels , it made perfect sense.

The Marvels ends with Monica Rambeau becoming trapped on the other side of a multiversal anomaly, with it being revealed that she has landed in another universe. There, she meets a variant of her mother, as well as Kelsey Grammer's Beast, setting up the return of the X-Men. While Rambeau's appearance in Doomsday hasn't been confirmed, this could very well be what causes the incursion, triggering the beginning of Doom's plan. It isn't known whether Marvel Studios was planning on bringing Doom in during the development of The Marvels , but if this setup was intentional, it would be one of the biggest moments leading into Doomsday .

Unfortunately, Captain America: Brave New World was a disappointment to many. It failed to live up to the previous Captain America films, and the overwhelming number of Hulk-related characters took away from Sam Wilson's first time in the spotlight as Cap. However, the film does set up Doomsday in two big ways. First, it began Sam's journey to form a new Avengers team, something that will undoubtedly be continued as he unites with characters like Ant-Man and Shang-Chi in Doomsday .

More importantly, Brave New World may tease the arrival of Doom. In the film's post-credits scene, The Leader warns Sam Wilson of an incoming threat. According to the villain, he has calculated that the multiverse exists and that something is coming that will cause the heroes of Earth to have to defend their universe. This is clearly alluding to Doom, as he is the only multiversal threat who has popped up since Brave New World 's release. While this warning is vague, it does point to the story of Doomsday , and the arrival of the MCU's next big bad.

The New Avengers seem to be major players in the story of Doomsday , and it all comes back to Thunderbolts* . In the film's post-credits scene, the team is made aware of a multiversal phenomenon that is occurring in space. While watching footage of the event, it is revealed that the Fantastic Four's ship is headed to Earth. Even after the release of The Fantastic Four: First Steps , we still don't know why the team left Earth-838 or how they did it, meaning that this will likely be revealed in Doomsday .

Since the Doomsday trailers have revealed that the Fantastic Four are aware of Victor von Doom, it seems likely that the team will travel to Earth-199999 with him. So, Thunderbolts* acts as a perfect setup for this storyline, while also explaining why the New Avengers get involved in the story of the film. However, we can't guarantee that Doom is on that ship.

The Fantastic Four: First Steps features the MCU's biggest Doom setup yet, as the character actually appears in the film. The movie's mid-credits scene takes place some time after the events of the film, with an older Franklin Richards displaying advanced intelligence. After walking away, Sue returns to find that Franklin is looking at Doom, who has taken his mask off.

This could very well be the moment that Doom reintroduces himself to the Fantastic Four, kicking off the events of Doomsday . This scene also implies that Doom is interested in Franklin, which makes sense considering how powerful the young boy is. This scene created more hype for Doom's arrival than anything that has come before, and it'll be interesting to see how the dynamic between Doom and the Fantastic Four is developed in Doomsday .

Oddly enough, the rerelease of 2019's Avengers: Endgame also features some major Doom setups. Avengers: Endgame Encore features multiple new scenes that lead into Doomsday , and each one sets up a major plot point for the upcoming film. Firstly, Endgame 's ending continues a little longer than it originally did. The new ending shows Loki arrive at Steve and Peggy's house in the past, proving that they will be important to Doomsday 's multiversal conflict. It is possible that Steve's time travel shenanigans could have caused an incursion, something that Loki and Doom are both trying to stop.

The second scene shows Bruce Banner recording a video log while he is in holding, continuing the events of Spider-Man: Brand New Day . Doom then arrives and teleports Hulk away, leaving runes behind. This sets up the idea that Doom is collecting powerful MCU heroes, a theory that VisionQuest further cements. Finally, a scene at the TVA shows that multiple universes are collapsing, setting the stage for Doom to arrive and change the multiverse forever.

What is your favorite MCU Doom setup so far? Let us know on the ComicBook Forum !

A recording of sex noises appeared to be played from the audience as Strictly judge Motsi Mabuse delivered her remarks about the performance of Delta Goodrem and partner Kai Widdrington.

articles.title: Tim Burton’s Batman Set-Up an Incredible Twist on a Classic DC Villain, But It Took 28 Years to Happen
articles.summary: Billy Dee Williams is best known for playing Lando Calrissian in Star Wars, appearing in The Empire Strikes Back, Return of the Jedi, and, most recently, The Rise of Skywalker. While he’ll always be beloved as Lando Calrissian, his performance as Harvey Dent in Tim Burton’s 1989 Batman film is one of his more underrated […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Billy Dee Williams is best known for playing Lando Calrissian in Star Wars , appearing in The Empire Strikes Back, Return of the Jedi, and, most recently, The Rise of Skywalker . While he’ll always be beloved as Lando Calrissian, his performance as Harvey Dent in Tim Burton’s 1989 Batman film is one of his more underrated roles and is worth checking out.

When Burton cast Billy Dee Williams for Batman , he planned to use Two-Face — Harvey Dent’s villainous alter ego — in a future film. Burton was intrigued by the cinematic potential of a Black Two-Face who, with the burn, could literally be “black and white”. However, the vision would not come to pass — although it may be followed up on in The Batman Pt. II with actor Brian Tyree Henry — when Joel Schumacher took over the franchise and cast Tommy Lee Jones in the role.

Billy Dee Williams would reprise his role as Two-Face in The Lego Batman Movie as part of the larger voice cast for the 2017 film. The Lego Batman Movie was Williams’ second time voice-acting for a Lego film, having lent his voice to The Lego Movie, where he reprised his role as Lando Calrissian. While several performances were done in the style of actors for The Lego Batman Movie — John Venzon’s Penguin in the style of Danny DeVito from Batman Returns and Doug Benson’s Bane in the style of Tom Hardy in The Dark Knight Rises — Williams was one of the few original actors to return for the project.

While Billy Dee Williams’s Harvey Dent had a smaller role in Batman , the original story treatment for Batman Returns expanded on the district attorney’s role. Sam Hamm, the writer of the successful Batman film, charted a path for Harvey Dent to become the villainous Two-Face in his original treatment. Unfortunately, Warner Bros. pushed for the Penguin over Two-Face. They wanted the Penguin as the primary antagonist, believing that the Penguin was Batman’s most recognizable foe, right after the Joker.

Burton was granted greater creative control with Batman Returns , having expressed frustration with interference from producers. Sam Hamm was then replaced by writer Daniel Waters, who was behind the dark comedy Heathers in 1988, and unlike Hamm, had no emotional attachment to Batman. Daniel Waters replaced Harvey Dent’s place in the script with an original character, Max Shreck, the industrialist behind the Penguin’s mayoral campaign in the film. By the next film, Burton was out , and so were any notions of a Black Two-Face.

In 2016, artist Joe Quinones pitched a comic book continuation of the 1989 Batman film universe to DC Comics, inspired by the success of similar runs at the time. Quinones’ rejected pitch included turning Billy Dee Williams’ Harvey Dent into Two-Face along with the inclusion of Batgirl. Quinones was hardly the first to propose such an undertaking — in 2019, Jim Lee acknowledged that many creatives proposed a comic book series to be set in the Burton-verse and that the book wasn’t completely out of the question.

True to Lee’s statement, the book would come to fruition in 2021 . Titled Batman ‘89 , DC Comics tapped original Batman screenwriter Sam Hamm to write, along with artist Joe Quinones to illustrate the series. It launched in August of 2021, running for six issues before its continuation, titled Batman ‘89: Echoes , came out in November 2023.

Retroactively referred to as Batman ‘89: Shadows , the turn of Harvey Dent to Two-Face in the Burton-verse comic is a wild one. Taking place following the events of Batman Returns , Harvey Dent vows to take down Batman and current police commissioner Jim Gordon. In Batman ‘89, Dent is engaged to Barbara Gordon, who initially agrees with his plan. The comic deviates from the well-known origin of Two-Face, choosing instead to have his face burned by an ill-placed fall near car batteries leaking sulfuric acid. Batman and the original character Drake rush him to the hospital, but the damage has been done. From there, he starts relying on a coin to make decisions, and his behavior starts resembling the erratic nature fans associate with Two-Face as a character.

By the run’s end, Harvey Dent is dead. Over the course of the comic, he wounds Harvey Bullock, kills Jim Gordon, discovers Batman’s secret identity, murders Carmine Falcone and numerous mob goons while framing others for the crime. For a moment towards the end, there’s a glimmer of hope for Harvey Dent — he flips a coin to choose between killing Batman and letting Batman reform him. There are suggestions that it was a trick coin, rigged by Batman, but Selina Kyle finds Two-Face’s own coin, suggesting otherwise. Still, Two-Face’s influence outlasts the character’s lifespan. The comic ends with Batman deciding whether or not to go on patrol by flipping a coin.

What would you have liked to see from Billy Dee Williams as Two-Face? Will the character take a similar route in The Batman Pt. II? Let us know in the comments below!

The third edition of the just concluded UTH Festival just ran Nov. 20 and 21 at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, on the west bank of the Nile opposite Cairo, attracting roughly 10,000 attendees, according to organizers. articles.title: Could Succession Get A Spinoff Show? Kieran Culkin Has a Hilariously Blunt Response
articles.summary: Three years after Succession's series finale, Kieran Culkin has addressed whether the show could return. The Oscar-winning actor, who played Roman Roy on HBO’s drama for four seasons, doesn't think the family needs another chapter. While he misses playing the character, he thinks the series ended exactly as it should. During an appearance on Heart […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Three years after Succession 's series finale, Kieran Culkin has addressed whether the show could return. The Oscar-winning actor, who played Roman Roy on HBO’s drama for four seasons, doesn't think the family needs another chapter. While he misses playing the character, he thinks the series ended exactly as it should. During an appearance on Heart Breakfast to promote The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , Culkin was asked whether Succession could return. "Of course not. I think that would be a terrible idea," Culkin said, according to Variety . "What are you hoping for? Cousin Greg: The Sitcom?"

Obviously, Culkin was referring to Nicholas Braun's Greg Hirsch, whose awkward attempts to climb the corporate ladder made him one of the show's funniest characters. Greg spent most of the series attached to Matthew Macfadyen's Tom Wambsgans, eventually coming out on the winning side of the family's power struggle. Kieran jokes, but there are plenty of TomGreg fans who would tune in for that premise.

Despite his objection to a spinoff, Culkin admitted that he misses playing Roman. He also revealed that creator Jesse Armstrong had pitched him three potential directions for a fifth season . However, once he realized how Season 4 would end, Culkin also believed it was time to end the series. Succession ended in 2023 with the Roy siblings losing control of Waystar Royco. The finale left some open questions about what happened next for the Roy siblings, but Culkin believes the story came to its natural conclusion. "But it ended perfectly. The way it was supposed to," Culkin said.

Culkin may not want another Succession , but there's another famous role he could revisit. He played Fuller McCallister, Kevin's Pepsi-loving cousin, in the first two Home Alone movies alongside his older brother, Macaulay Culkin. With Macaulay reportedly developing a new Home Alone sequel with Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg , there’s also a chance to see how Fuller turned out as an adult. Kieran recently admitted to Jimmy Fallon that he still watches Home Alone almost every Christmas and that it is second only to Die Hard as his favorite holiday movie. We don’t know if he’s been invited to stay in the hide-a-bed in the attic yet, but an on-screen reunion of the brothers would certainly lock in the nostalgia.

Kieran hasn't reprised the role of Fuller since Home Alone 2 in 1992, though his brother recently returned as Kevin in a new McDonald's commercial . In the meantime, Culkin is working on a different reunion. He's preparing to work with Succession creator Jesse Armstrong on a new movie. "I'm about to work with Jesse on a movie. He wrote something," Culkin said, without offering further details. Armstrong recently made his feature directorial debut with HBO's Mountainhead . The film was a dark comedy about four billionaire friends navigating a global crisis they created while vacationing at a mountain retreat. It's not another season of Succession , but at least it gives fans something to look forward to while they wait for TomGreg: The Sitcom .
